title: Flux curvature does not give a visit-robust signal in 19 selected dusty dwarfs
abstract: We test whether the W1 versus W2 flux relation departs from a straight line in 19 published infrared-variable dwarfs with a positive estimated W2 excess. A fixed spectrum with changing area gives a straight relation. We prove that fixed-area thermal emission gives a convex relation in monochromatic bands, and in separated positive passbands under stated assumptions. Fits allow errors in both bands and seasonal offsets. With a 0.01 mag error floor, G4466 alone exceeds a conditional 19-star simulation threshold. Its score improvement is 17.52, with group tail estimate 0.018. Removal of its first visit lowers the improvement to 5.48; a 0.02 mag floor lowers it to 6.49. Its fitted curvature is negative, opposite to simple heating, but the evidence is sensitive to these changes. No source remains above the full-data threshold after every single-visit deletion. This does not prove fixed temperature. Limits include prior source selection, assumed errors, no new observations and exclusion of one parent source with no positive W2 excess and unstable weak-signal fits. We preserve code, aggregate results, proof, source hashes and reproduction steps. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-626f0f4a2a20; topic astronomy; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.
